newsitem.title: UK: New LME options seen having advantages over OTC.
newsitem.headline: New LME options seen having advantages over OTC.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) traded average price options (TAPOs), due to be launched at the end of January 1997, will have several advantages over off-exchange average rate "Asian" options, metals consultant David Ward said.

Members trading TAPOs will benefit from better price transparency, with the LME publishing daily valuations for closing prices of TAPOs with corresponding Notional Average Futures Prices for 27 months, he told an LME Seminar on Monday.
"The LME will provide an independent benchmark for the industry," he said.
The introduction is also expected to increase liquidity and enhance market efficiency, he said.
"TAPOs will provide members with a new market to trade out of unwanted risk," he said.

"This is in contrast to the current situation where members have to conjure with a combination of traded options and futures contracts to manufacture a partial offset against their Asian options," Ward added.
He said an additional arbitrage market between standard traded options and TAPOs could also develop.
Greater liquidity would arise from new entrants into the market, including members and customers restricted in their use of off-exchange products.
The third area where TAPOs are seen as having advantages over Asian options was security, Ward said.
"By clearing trades through the London Clearing House, Members trading TAPOs minimise the risk of a counterparty default," he said.
He also said a TAPO contract, "would be expected to compare favourably with an off exchange product" in terms of capital adequacy requirements.
Ward said a survey from LME members suggested around 70 percent of current Asian option business was done in copper and 25 percent in aluminium.
This was the reason for launching TAPO contracts for these two metals, he said.
